meta.notes: Rough planning numbers, checked 2026-11-23. All money values are USD (per million tokens, per GPU-hour, per month, per kWh or per item); US prices exclude sales tax, EU/Swedish prices converted from EUR/SEK are noted per item with their VAT status. Hardware, RAM and GPU-rental prices were rising fast in late 2025-2026 because of a memory-chip shortage; API prices change monthly. Image, video and speech prices (media_api, media_closed) are USD per picture, megapixel, second of video, 1,000 characters or minute or hour of audio, as each offer states. Sources and caveats are in pricing-notes.md.

usage_profiles.label: A few questions a day
usage_profiles.basis: About 2.5 billion ChatGPT messages a day from about 700 million weekly users in mid-2025, i.e. roughly 3-4 messages per weekly user per day (UNU summary of the Harvard/Duke/OpenAI usage study, https://c3.unu.edu/projects/ai/infographic/easyread_howtheworlduseschatgpt.html). Input includes the system prompt and earlier turns of the conversation; output is a typical answer of 400-500 words. People at the same moment: about 1 in 10 users is waiting for an answer at the same moment in working hours, because a few short questions are spread over the day (assumption, not measured). Rough.

usage_profiles.label: Daily work assistant (writing, email, questions)
usage_profiles.basis: OpenRouter/a16z State of AI (100 trillion tokens, Nov 2024-Nov 2025, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.10088v1): average prompt grew from about 1,500 to over 6,000 tokens and average completion from about 150 to 400 tokens; programming prompts average 3-4x general prompts and make up over half of the tokens, which puts a general-purpose prompt at about 4,000 tokens. Output raised to 600 because completions keep growing with reasoning models. 30 requests is a full working day of regular use. People at the same moment: about 1 in 5 users at busy times in working hours, for regular use through the day (assumption, not measured). Rough.

usage_profiles.label: Coding assistant, heavy use
usage_profiles.basis: Claude Code docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs): enterprise average about $13 per developer per active day ($150-250 a month), under $30 for 90% of users. The docs' example session has 940k cached input, 50k cache writes, 1.2k uncached input and 5.3k output tokens, i.e. agents resend a large, mostly cached context with every tool call and write little. 400 requests x 50,000 input tokens (about 94% cache reads) x 300 output tokens comes to about $12 a day at the Sonnet-class prices that example used ($3/$15, cache read $0.30, cache write $3.75). OpenRouter's study also says code requests routinely exceed 20,000 input tokens. Assumes 22 active (working) days a month, as for every profile. Cost depends heavily on cache pricing. People at the same moment: about 2 in 5 developers have a request running at the same moment, because a coding agent sends long chains of requests while the developer works (assumption, not measured). Rough.

usage_profiles.label: Reading and summarising documents
usage_profiles.basis: Claude PDF docs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support): each PDF page typically uses 1,500-3,000 text tokens; OpenAI (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/4936856-what-are-tokens-and-how-to-count-them): about 100 tokens per 75 English words. 25,000 tokens is about 18,000 English words (at 100 tokens per 75 words), or roughly 8 to 17 PDF pages at 1,500-3,000 tokens a page; the 800-token summary is about 600 words. Ten documents a day. Swedish and other non-English text uses more tokens per word. media_closed.product: gpt-realtime-2.1-mini (successor to the deprecated TTS models)
media_closed.unit_detail: per minute of generated speech, audio output tokens only
media_closed.note: OpenAI has deprecated tts-1 ($15 per million characters), tts-1-hd ($30 per million characters) and gpt-4o-mini-tts ($12 per million audio tokens); all shut down on 6 January 2027, and OpenAI says to migrate to gpt-realtime-2.1-mini on the Realtime API. Its audio output costs $20 per million tokens; OpenAI's Realtime cost guide states assistant audio is 1 token per 50 ms, so 1,200 tokens a minute x $20 / 1,000,000 = $0.024 per minute. Text input ($0.60 per million tokens) and any conversation context re-sent each turn come on top, and it is a conversational model rather than a plain speech endpoint.
